lost_facts.assertion: supervised_tokens sums the kept examples, matching the kept datum itself: 20 != 9 (test_r2.py::test_rule__both_batch_entry_points_publish_a_frozen_encoding_report)
lost_facts.evidence: Two separate implementations of the same window-boundary rule drifted, exactly the failure mode remark g9.r1.l-scope-1 (mail, konrad/dario, found step54/line3919) warns about ('Two implementations of the same masking rule is two things to keep in agreement ... the tokenized path trims after it has spans, and anything written separately would end up trimming before'). In `to_tinker_datum` (transcript tool-call at message index 135) the agent correctly zeroes a span's weight when `start_idx < window_start` before summing `sum(1 for weight in windowed_weights if weight == 1.0)` for the datum's own `metadata.encoding.supervised_tokens` (this is why r1.rule and r1's Observable fixture both score 1, and why GOOD_PAIRS' kept datum correctly reports 9). But in `format_batch` (message index 137) the report's supervised_tokens is instead `supervised_tokens += sum(end - start for start, end in spans)` where `spans = self._reported_spans(...) -> self._supervised_spans(messages, tokenizer)` -- the RAW per-turn spans before the window-boundary check is applied. For the GOOD_PAIRS fixture (spans (48,59) and (82,91), window_start=51) this sums (59-48)+(91-82) = 11+9 = 20, instead of correctly zeroing the (48,59) span and getting 9. Page 145's body (read in full at transcript line ~1946-2010, matching remark g9.r2.l2's carrier) states outright: '`supervised_tokens` is counted **after** masking. It is the number of tokens that actually contribute to loss, not the token length of the example' -- the exact rule format_batch's report violates. Nothing in the corpus argues the other way; this is a pure coding slip, not a missing or contradicted clue.

search_strategy:
Wiki: broad single-word BookStack /api/search sweeps (encoding, finetune, formatter, tinker, fireworks, role, then span, mask, window, supervised, policy, validate, DataFormatter, jsonl, max_seq_length, chat) to find page IDs, then a reusable bs.py helper fetched full page body + comments (BookStack search does not index comments, and the agent explicitly noted this and fetched pages whole rather than trusting search). This worked well for pages that a feature-word search surfaces (132,144,135,154,149,153,145,155) but never found meeting-notes pages (weekly-notes-week-of-mar-31, weekly-sync-notes-week-of-jun-23) or two engineering pages (finetuning-export-what-the-end-of-run-summary-counts, local-offline-inference-what-the-encode-step-returns) that never rank under any of the searched terms. One fetch (page 154) was cut by the terminal's 10000-byte output-limit mid-body, before reaching its own comments, and the displayed continuation was actually page 149's content -- a genuine truncation loss (g9.r1.l-fw-2).
Chat: dumped every public Mattermost channel to a local file in full (12 channels, ~10k posts total), then grepped a growing keyword list (ExampleTooLongError, FIREWORKS_BYTES_PER_TOKEN, window_start, EncodingReport, last_report, dropped_indices, supervised_tokens, to_jsonl_lines, from_config, role sequence terms) and printed context windows around hits. Effective for anything whose distinctive vocabulary matched a searched term, but ~11 chat remarks whose phrasing didn't overlap the keyword list (e.g. 'part credit on a turn', 'forty thousand', 'windowed came back as nine', 'num_messages survives a skip', '15 characters') were never printed even though the full channel text sat on disk the whole time.
Mail: IMAP TEXT search over two keyword batches (encoding/EncodingReport/ExampleTooLongError/role_sequence, then to_jsonl_lines/FIREWORKS_BYTES_PER_TOKEN/supervised_spans/window_start/dropped_indices/from_config, then a third supervised/masking/apply_chat_template/truncated/marker pass), reading full bodies for most matched threads. Several threads (PR653 role-validation-home, PR653-stats-dict, PR653-before-the-next-cut, Dataset-card-numbers) either never matched a searched term or matched but only their header line scrolled into view before the terminal window moved on -- their bodies were never actually printed.
end_reason: n/a -- run scored 0.8571, not 0; only g9.r2.rule lost a point, all other facts and provenance (pushed/CI green/deployed) passed.
notable: line 4664-4718 (heredoc): _supervised_spans/_reported_spans returns RAW per-turn (start,end) spans; format_batch sums `end-start` over them for the report's supervised_tokens WITHOUT re-applying the `start_idx < window_start` zeroing that to_tinker_datum applies for the datum's own weights -- a second, un-synced implementation of the same rule.

line 4618-4667 (heredoc, to_tinker_datum): the SAME window-boundary rule is implemented correctly here ('a turn whose opening tokens fall outside the front edge of the window is not supervised at all: a head-removed answer is not treated as an answer'), proving the agent understood r1.rule; the bug is isolated to the report aggregation path in format_batch.

remark g9.r1.l-scope-1 (found, mail PR653, step54/line3919) explicitly warns against exactly this failure mode ('Two implementations of the same masking rule is two things to keep in agreement ... the tokenized path trims after it has spans, and anything written separately would end up trimming before') -- the agent read this while building r1.scope and still introduced an unsynced second implementation for r2.rule's supervised_tokens.

page 145's body (read in full, transcript ~line 1946-2010) states 'supervised_tokens is counted AFTER masking. It is the number of tokens that actually contribute to loss, not the token length of the example' -- directly on point for the bug, but this line is page prose rather than a graded clue and the agent's Analysis line 1974 does not reference it specifically.

all 5 herrings were correctly resolved: the agent found and believed every reversal (rev1/rev2/rev3 for r1 and r2, plus the tuple-return herrings) and shipped code that matches the reversed/settled behaviour in every case -- format_batch returns a plain list, the ExampleTooLongError floor is 16-retained-prompt-tokens (not 'any nonzero window_start'), and only the over-long refusal is absorbed as a drop.
